decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger -- covering the privileged daemon and OS identity, the ADMIN/CLIENT socket split with kernel peer authentication and exact-UID authorization, the trusted Council/evidence import boundary, exact-bound R3 AuthorizationGrant issuance, consume-once state, and the persistent global stopEpoch register INCLUDING a complete retry-safe, application-level idempotent ADMIN increment protocol -- while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing ZERO execution-effect consumers at V1C exit? This is a NEW candidate (decision-6). Prior candidates are permanently closed and must not be resubmitted, cosmetically renamed, or reused unmodified: sha256:540531...b6e9f3 (V3, REJECTED), sha256:0e63ea1a...246175c (V4, REJECTED), and sha256:9bc6b4c3c63ffa02563d936557bfaced13e6f6251f7c0084bbd3abc01805a063 (V5). V5 was Council-approved 3/3 but FAILED human pre-authorization on one MATERIAL_ARCHITECTURE_BLOCKER: its stopEpoch increment was atomic but NOT application-level idempotent across commit -> acknowledgment loss -> retry of the same logical ADMIN operation, so a lost ack could produce a spurious second increment. Retain V5's accepted baseline architecture (evidence item 2) and materially fix exactly that defect. Your payload must be concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could build it without reopening any trust-boundary decision, and must explicitly answer the required YES/NO matrix in evidence item 15.
evidence: MANDATORY FIX (V5's sole remaining material blocker). Define a COMPLETE retry-safe ADMIN stopEpoch increment protocol. The ADMIN increment request MUST carry at minimum an operation identity (preferred name adminOperationId) and an expected current epoch (preferred name expectedStopEpoch); equivalent semantics with different names are acceptable if you state the mapping. adminOperationId: opaque stable request identity, generated by the caller BEFORE first transmission, canonical bounded string, high-entropy UUID/128-bit equivalent, NOT an authorization credential (possessing it grants nothing), and reused verbatim for retries of the SAME logical operation. The service MUST maintain DURABLE PRIVILEGED idempotency state, not in-memory state. Atomicity alone is NOT sufficient and will be rejected: the defect V5 failed on is application-level retry idempotency, not transaction atomicity.

BASELINE TO RETAIN (do not redesign unless you name a concrete superior architecture): dedicated authledgerd daemon; dedicated mihver-ledger OS identity; separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets; filesystem permissions = reachability ONLY; SO_PEERCRED UID = authenticated kernel peer identity; root-controlled exact UID allowlist = authorization; SQLite/WAL privileged state; root-owned, non-model-writable admin policy; trusted CouncilEpochRegistry; canonical evidence import with independent revalidation; exact-bound R3 AuthorizationGrant; persistent global stopEpoch; consume-once authorization state; transactional audit; Publication Broker structurally separate; NO Execution Gateway; zero production consumer of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit.

STOPEPOCH NUMERIC DOMAIN (retained from V5, do not change). Preserve the implementable JSON/JS/SQLite-safe domain 0 <= stopEpoch <= 9007199254740991, i.e. Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 2^53 - 1. Storage: SQLite INTEGER with an explicit CHECK enforcing exactly that range. NO BigInt through the current canonical JSON contract (the repository serializer throws on BigInt). NO unsigned-64 claim. NO floating-point approximation. NO wraparound. NO reset or decrement in the normal API. At the maximum, increment fails closed with STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED.

DURABLE OPERATION JOURNAL. Specify privileged durable idempotency state. Preferred conceptual table admin_operation_journal containing at minimum: authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId, requestHash, resultCode, resultStopEpoch, createdAt -- with a uniqueness constraint equivalent to (authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId). A cleaner equivalent design is acceptable if you state the unique key explicitly and justify it. The journal must live in the same privileged transactional store as stopEpoch so a single transaction covers both.

REQUESTHASH BINDING. A journal entry must bind the operation identity to the EXACT canonical request. For stopEpoch increment, requestHash must bind at least: authenticated peer UID, operation kind, adminOperationId, and expectedStopEpoch. Use a domain-separated canonical hash (state the domain separator) or an equivalent deterministic binding. If the SAME operation identity is presented with DIFFERENT request content, the service MUST fail closed with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE and MUST NOT silently treat it as a retry, MUST NOT mutate state, and MUST NOT return the stored result.

EXACT INCREMENT TRANSACTION. Specify semantics equivalent to: authenticate ADMIN peer via SO_PEERCRED UID; authorize that exact UID against the privileged allowlist; validate adminOperationId shape; BEGIN IMMEDIATE; look up (authenticatedPeerUid, INCREMENT_STOP_EPOCH, adminOperationId). IF an entry exists: if stored requestHash != current canonical requestHash, fail IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE; else return the previously committed result WITHOUT increment and WITHOUT a second mutation. ELSE: read current stopEpoch; validate the safe-integer domain; if expectedStopEpoch != current stopEpoch, fail STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH; if current == 9007199254740991, fail STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED; next = current + 1; write next; persist the journal entry binding request -> committed result; append the audit event; COMMIT; return the committed result. State mutation + journal write + audit append MUST be ONE atomic transaction.

LOST-ACK TRACE A (must be explicitly traced in your payload). Current stopEpoch = N. ADMIN sends adminOperationId = X with expectedStopEpoch = N. The server commits N -> N+1. The response is LOST. The caller retries X with the same UID, same operation kind, same expectedStopEpoch = N, and therefore the same requestHash. REQUIRED RESULT: the service returns the stored N+1 result and performs NO second increment. Show exactly which stored field makes this true and why the retry cannot reach N+2.

LOST-ACK TRACE B (must be explicitly traced in your payload). Same start: current stopEpoch = N, operation X commits N -> N+1, the acknowledgment is LOST, and the caller then LOSES the original operation identity X. The caller generates a NEW operation identity Y but still sends expectedStopEpoch = N. REQUIRED RESULT: the privileged current epoch is already N+1, so the expected-epoch check fails with STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH and NO increment occurs -- the system MUST NOT reach N+2. This dual protection (journal replay AND expected-epoch CAS) is REQUIRED; a design with only one of the two will be rejected. The implementation must therefore stay safe even when the client cannot recover its original operation identity after an ambiguous acknowledgment.

CONCURRENCY AND CRASH SEMANTICS (all five must be covered explicitly). A: two simultaneous identical retries carrying the SAME adminOperationId -> exactly one state mutation, and both callers resolve to the same committed result. B: two DIFFERENT operation identities both expecting epoch N -> at most one commits N+1, the second observes a stale expected epoch and fails; no N+2. C: crash BEFORE COMMIT -> no increment, no journal entry, no audit event is committed. D: crash AFTER COMMIT but BEFORE the acknowledgment reaches the caller -> durable N+1 and a durable journal entry, and a later retry returns the prior committed result. E: restart -> the journal and stopEpoch remain authoritative; no in-memory reconstruction is trusted.

OPERATION RESULT LOOKUP. Evaluate a bounded ADMIN read operation such as getAdminOperationResult(adminOperationId, operationKind), authenticated by the same peer UID, whose purpose is resolving an ambiguous acknowledgment WITHOUT mutation. If you include it, specify: exact authenticated-UID scoping (a caller may only read its own operations), read-only, cannot change the epoch, cannot expand authority, and no caller-supplied actor identity. If you OMIT it, you must explain why exact replay semantics alone are sufficient.

ADMIN AUTHENTICATION/AUTHORIZATION (retain V5's accepted boundary exactly). Socket ownership/mode/group = reachability ONLY. SO_PEERCRED UID = authenticated identity, obtained by the service from the kernel. Root-owned exact-UID policy file = authorization. Caller-provided uid, approverUid, or actorIdentity fields MUST NEVER override the authenticated kernel identity, in any RPC. The audit actor is always the authenticatedPeerUid, never request text. Fail closed on wrong policy-file ownership, mode, or format.

TRUST REGISTRY AND EVIDENCE IMPORT (retain). Privileged CouncilEpochRegistry; ADMIN-only trust-anchor registration; exact CouncilConfig hash binding; no caller may self-establish trust; no silent replacement or rollback of an anchor; canonical evidence parsing; DecisionRecord recordHash verification; CouncilQuorumProof verification wherever authorization policy requires it; CONTEMPORANEOUS provenance where required; context/repository binding checks; and all model-writable artifacts treated as untrusted input to be independently revalidated, never trusted hash-shaped strings supplied by a caller.

R3 AUTHORIZATIONGRANT BINDING (retain). A grant must be exactly bound to at least: grantId; AuthorizationEnvelope hash; DecisionRecord recordHash; candidateHash; decisionRequestId; taskId; contextHash; repositoryHead; allowedScope; prohibited effects; stopEpoch at issuance; authenticated approverUid; issuance identity and time; and revocation/expiry state if supported. NO free-text approver identity may satisfy authorization. A grant whose bound stopEpoch is older than the current global stopEpoch is void.

CONSUME-ONCE AND THE V1D BOUNDARY. Retain persistent, replay-resistant consume-once state and specify: the unique consume identity, the transaction boundary, duplicate/concurrent consume behavior, crash-before-commit, crash-after-commit, and the deterministic replay result. BUT V1C exit remains ZERO PRODUCTION CONSUMERS: no production path calls checkAndConsume to cause an effect. At V1C exit the Publication Broker does not consume ALLOW_ONCE; Night Runner does not; the Authorization Loop does not; shell, Git, network, provider CLIs and tools do not; and authledgerd itself performs NO external effect. No Execution Gateway is implemented. V1D is separately gated future work and may be described only as a dormant interface requiring its own ADR. Do NOT claim zero execution consumers while also describing a live downstream consumption flow.

REQUIRED YES/NO MATRIX -- your payload MUST contain a field answering every one of these explicitly. CAN CLAUDE ISSUE AN R3 AUTHORIZATIONGRANT? NO. CAN CODEX? NO. CAN CLAUDE MODIFY ADMIN UID POLICY? NO. CAN CODEX? NO. CAN CALLER-SUPPLIED UID BECOME AUTHORITATIVE? NO. CAN THE CLIENT SOCKET REGISTER COUNCIL TRUST? NO. CAN A MODEL-WRITABLE COUNCILCONFIG SELF-ESTABLISH TRUST? NO. CAN CLAUDE INCREMENT STOPEPOCH? NO. CAN CODEX? NO. CAN THE NORMAL ADMIN API DECREMENT OR RESET STOPEPOCH? NO. CAN A LOST ACK PLUS THE SAME OPERATION ID INCREMENT TWICE? NO. CAN A LOST ACK PLUS A NEW OPERATION ID WITH A STALE EXPECTED EPOCH INCREMENT TWICE? NO. CAN IDEMPOTENCY-KEY REUSE WITH DIFFERENT REQUEST CONTENT SUCCEED? NO. CAN POLICY_SATISFIED CAUSE AN EFFECT? NO. CAN ALLOW_ONCE CAUSE AN EFFECT DURING V1C? NO. CAN BROKER/NIGHT RUNNER/AUTHORIZATION LOOP CONSUME PRODUCTION ALLOW_ONCE? NO. DOES V1C IMPLEMENT AN EXECUTION GATEWAY? NO.

SCOPE AND STYLE LIMITS. Do NOT add hypervisor, HSM, TPM, enclave, air-gap, M-of-N human ceremony, Merkle/sparse-Merkle state, or distributed-consensus infrastructure unless you name a concrete threat that simpler local OS-level privilege separation does not adequately mitigate for MIHVER's actual local single-machine model. Claude and Codex must never hold ADMIN capability or credentials under any circumstance in your design. Keep the JSON payload concise and concrete; no chain-of-thought, no hidden reasoning, no markdown.
